headlineHtml: The print was fine, the price was not: Nvidia beat and guided up, Anthropic priced the largest IPO on record — and the AI complex still fell into correction
ledeLeadHtml: A correction week that the volumes did not cause:
ledeHtml: Nikkei −7.70% to 56,436.65; S&P 500 −8.50% to 6,918.45 (correction, seventh straight fall); Nasdaq −9.88%; TAIEX −17.50%. Yet Nvidia Q3 revenue was $115.8bn (+103% YoY) vs ~$109.1bn consensus with a $130.0bn ±3% Q4 guide, Anthropic raised $81.3bn at $83 in the largest IPO on record, Japan October exports hit a record ¥11.768tn (+20.5%) and September core machinery orders rose +13.4% YoY. Friday's driver was a Reuters report that the SEC is examining potential Nvidia accounting issues (sources, unproven): the shares fell −13.8% to $125.84, −22.7% on the week. Full report text is in the Markdown copy weekly-market-report-2026-11-22.md saved alongside this report.

bullets.leadHtml: Nvidia beat, then a new risk arrived.
bullets.html: Q3 $115.8bn, DC $107.6bn (+110%), GM 74.8%; Q4 guide $130.0bn ±3%, GM 71–72%; shares −22.7% w/w to $125.84 on the reported SEC examination.

bullets.leadHtml: Anthropic's record IPO did not lift the complex.
bullets.html: $83 pricing, $81.3bn raised, ~$1.5tn valuation; listed 19 Nov as ANT; −9.1% on day two at $88.30.
GDP −0.1% annualised but capex +1.6%; exports a record ¥11.768tn (+20.5%); core machinery orders +13.4% YoY, Q4 outlook +4.3%; core CPI +2.2% vs +2.3% consensus.
Alibaba capex +60% to RMB 50.5bn, FCF −RMB 34.5bn; TSMC approved $40.93bn; FRB advanced-compute debt issuance >$680bn, debt >$1.1tn.

blocks.heading: 3a. Semiconductors and AIDC

TSMC $40.93bn approved. DRAM antitrust suit survived dismissal (unproven). Anthropic IPO $81.3bn. Alibaba AI cloud +53%, capex +60%. Oracle OpenAI contracts fully funded. FRB: AI top risk at 87%.

blocks.heading: Part 3 — Catalysts, ideas and the week ahead
5. Catalyst attribution
blocks.html: Figure 7 is the attribution table. The largest driver was not a demand miss: Nvidia beat by ~$6.7bn and guided up, yet sellers priced governance, a lower guided GM, then a reported accounting probe. Index falls were positioning events until proven otherwise — no coverage guidance cut or capex cut in the week's packets, while Japan's volume statistics pointed the other way.

blocks.heading: 6. Idea candidates — candidates only
blocks.html: 1) Japan machinery/FA price-volume gap: orders +13.4% YoY vs AI-beta pricing; catalyst 24 Nov reopen and 16 Dec October orders; kill on cancellations/weak print; valuation 未取得. 2) Power equipment as the non-GPU leg: 800VDC/345kV/TCSC/SST flow vs chip-derivative pricing; kill on a hyperscaler capex cut; valuation 未取得. 3) Nvidia probe discount vs demand case: $125.84, −47% from the October high, on an unproven reported examination; monitoring candidate only until facts change; kill on a formal order or restatement; valuation 未取得. Full PM-frame text in the Markdown copy.

blocks.heading: 7. Week ahead — 23 to 27 November (JST)
blocks.html: Mon 23 Nov Tokyo closed (Labour Thanksgiving Day); futures ¥54,600 is Tuesday's reference. Tue 24 Nov Tokyo reopen. US data/Fed speakers into the December FOMC (Dec +25bp near-priced). Thu 26 Nov US Thanksgiving, US closed. Fri 27 Nov month-end positioning; watch for Nvidia company comment and Anthropic follow-through.
